title: CAT 2022 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Sequence and Series
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: For any natural number $n$, suppose the sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression is $(n + 2n^2)$. If the $n^{th}$ term of the progression is divisible by 9, then the smallest possible value of $n$ is
questions.explain: The sum of the first $n$ terms is $S_n = 2n^2 + n$. The $n^{th}$ term is $T_n = S_n - S_{n-1} = 2n^2+n - (2(n-1)^2 + (n-1)) = 4n - 1$. We want $4n - 1$ to be divisible by 9. Testing options: For $n=7$, $4(7)-1 = 27$, which is divisible by 9. Therefore, 7 is the smallest possible value.
